correctness.rationale: Exact triple-terminal tree-path union gives conditional pair kernel. originality.rationale: The established multivariate tree product-distance inverse (Bapat–Sivasubramanian 2012, Thm. 2.2) was identified and is NOT claimed as new. The actual final claim combines a separately verified three-terminal infection-event factorization, path-supported transformation of the two-alarm event, and exact elimination of an arbitrary source distribution; inspected source-localization and tree-SIR primary treatments do not state it. Residual risk: a related identity may exist under reliability or tree-process terminology; no independent bibliographic certification.
residual_risks: The inverse product-distance identity is prior art; separate novelty rests solely on the path-local paired-event consequence, potentially known as a tree reliability identity.
The 2006 original paper was not fully accessible; its known technical theorem was crosschecked through the 2012 full paper.
Accessible portions and document-wide searches of the Markovian tree-SIR paper cannot prove complete noncoverage of every equivalent statistical identity.
Search-result absence does not establish uniqueness; no independent originality audit.

value.rationale: For a specified unknown single-source distribution, every pairwise joint monitor-alarm probability can be computed exactly from only individual monitor rates along the connecting path. This reduces all O(n^2) paired measurements to n marginals, gives exact model-consistency tests, and reveals off-path irrelevance for arbitrary heterogeneous tree bonds. The specific probabilistic cancellation has a motivated epidemiological interpretation distinct from its algebraic inverse lemma.
